about: A Zork II-style cave adventure. You start sealed in a barrow, go through a cavern with a wizard who pops in and out, and reach a garden with a gazebo. Treasures lie further south, past a pearl door with a riddle and a room that will not keep still.

done.why: I took a short sample of the opening and stopped before reaching any puzzle.

moments.note: The Wizard reads my empty hands and gives directions to the treasure.
The room 'settles down and is only a room'. I did not know what that meant.
Stabbing the unicorn with a lantern got a witty reply that sounded like a verdict on my character.
A politely phrased request to the sword was not understood.

wished: To interact with the grue on the bridge
To be able to read the Zork I copy

lines.line: The unicorn, unsurprised by this evidence that you are indeed the uncouth sort of vagabond it suspected you were, melts into the hedges and is gone.
lines.why: The world responded to my odd action with a joke.

lines.line: His eye goes to your hands, which hold nothing he values, and he relaxes a little
lines.why: The wizard reacted to what I was carrying.

fun.why: Some witty responses, but I played only briefly.

engagement.why: The hints at a room that will not keep still made me curious.

difficulty.why: I did not get far enough to judge.

interestingness.why: A Zork pastiche that responds to what you carry and what you do.
